object_description: three cleverly positioned new buildings framing a raised school square and a lower school park
design_condition: three precisely positioned buildings continue the village structure, framing a higher school square with the classroom buildings and a lower school park with the public buildings, mediating between terrace and plain

positive: The village structure is continued spatially and strengthened by three cleverly positioned new buildings
Their precise positioning preserves the long-distance effect of the existing wing and helps the 1960s wing to a convincing appearance
A new strong expression with its own character is clearly established
The park-like open space and informal walkway skilfully reinterpret the altered topography
Differentiated outdoor, intermediate and retreat spaces mediate between terrace and plain
The handling of topography and wooded volumes is skilful at all scales
The positioning of the entrances mediates between the two levels
The placement of trees creates clear zoning and harmonious networking of landscape and settlement space
Many differently sunlit or shaded, versatile open spaces are generated
The different paths allow a fine-meshed permeability
The related new buildings form independent addresses yet stay clearly subordinate to the buildings worth preserving
They quote existing vocabulary through volumetric proportions and the grounding plinth
The main entrance widens into a lounge that encourages encounters
Teaching floors are built around a central studio zone forming a convincing learning and meeting space
Basement workrooms with outdoor spaces in front are also open to the public
Consistent separation allows flawless parallel school and public operations
The high proportion of wood promises comfortable rooms and low grey energy
Grid-like floor plans and consistent system separation guarantee durable, adaptable rooms
Widely overhanging roofs and an appropriate window proportion ensure summer thermal protection
Volumetry and settlement along the site edge reduce excavation volume and pit stabilisation
The staging allows construction without temporary solutions and without disrupting school operations
The volumes rewrite the village at a scale suitable for children and appropriate to the site
Permeable open spaces read as a natural sequence of squares and park-like spaces where school and public uses coexist
negative: The gymnasium building sits relatively deep in the ground and will require buoyancy stabilisation measures
The proposed additional teaching unit may weaken the intention of subordinating the new buildings to the existing wing
